name: Ocean
facts: The ocean covers about 71% of Earth's surface.
More than 80% of the ocean is unmapped and unexplored in detail.
The Mariana Trench is about 11 kilometres deep at its deepest point, the Challenger Deep.
If Mount Everest were placed in the Mariana Trench, its peak would still be more than 2 kilometres underwater.
Phytoplankton in the ocean produce a large share of the oxygen we breathe, often estimated at around half.
The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on Earth and can be seen from space.
The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived, bigger than any dinosaur.
The Pacific Ocean is larger than all of Earth's land area combined.
Some jellyfish species, like Turritopsis dohrnii, can revert to an earlier life stage, earning the nickname 'immortal jellyfish'.
Seawater is salty mostly because of minerals washed from rocks on land by rivers.
The longest mountain range on Earth is underwater: the mid-ocean ridge, about 65,000 kilometres long.
Sound travels about four times faster in water than in air.
Many deep-sea creatures make their own light, a process called bioluminescence.
The Atlantic Ocean widens by a few centimetres every year as tectonic plates move apart.
Female sea turtles return to the same region where they hatched to lay their own eggs.
Coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean floor but support around a quarter of all marine species.
The deepest part of the ocean is in complete darkness; sunlight barely reaches below about 1,000 metres.
An octopus can change both the colour and the texture of its skin in a fraction of a second.
The Dead Sea is so salty that people float on it easily.
Sharks have existed for more than 400 million years, longer than trees.
The Gulf Stream is a powerful ocean current that carries warm water from the tropics north along the coast of North America.
Seahorse fathers, not mothers, carry the eggs and give birth.
Dolphins sleep with one half of their brain at a time so they can keep breathing.
The ocean absorbs roughly a quarter of the carbon dioxide that humans release.
Tides are caused mainly by the Moon's gravity pulling on Earth's oceans.
